sentences.text:
Sewakram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 February, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Jbp:10426
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice B. P. Sharma
 On The 5 th Of February, 2026
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 35578 of 2023
 Sewakram And Others
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Ramraj Chauhan - Advocate for the petitioner.
 Shri Vishnu Prasad- Advocate for respondent Nos. 2 to 5

Order 
This petition has been filed by the petitioners being aggrieved by the proceedings of Order dated 11.07.23 passed in ST No. 197/22 by II ASJ Balaghat whereby application U/s 320(2) of Cr.P.C filed by respondent Nos. 2 to 5 have been rejected, and proceedings have been initiated against the petitioners.

2. It is submitted that police has filed the charge-sheet against the petitioners under Sections 406,
420, 120-B of IPC and 21(3) of Banning of Irregular Deposit Scheme Adhiniyam, 2019 which is pending before the trial Court for consideration.
3.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is further submitted that in the meanwhile, the parties have entered into settlement.
Their statements have been recorded before the Registry., which are available on record.
As per the statements of the parties, they settled the matter and the complainant stated that they have received the amount.
The petitioners also stated that they have made payment to the complainant and they have no objection to compromise the matter.
4. Perusal of the record reflects that the petitioners have entered into a compromise with the complainants and Registry has also verified the compromise application.

In the case of State of M.P.
vs. Laxmi Narayan (2019) 5 SCC 688, a Three NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10426 2 MCRC-35578-2023 Judge Bench of the Apex Court discussed the earlier judgments of the Apex Court and laid down the principles in para-15.

State of M.P.
vs. Laxmi Narayan (2019) 5 SCC 688
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant para-15.1 & 15.2 are reproduced as under:-
''15.1 That the power conferred under Section 482 of the Code to quash the criminal proceedings for the non-compoundable offences under Section 320 of the Code can Sewakram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128864858/
1 be exercised having overwhelmingly and predominantly the civil character,
particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes and when the parties have resolved the entire dispute amongst themselves; 15.2.

entities.text: Sewakram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such power is not to be exercised in those prosecutions which involved heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc.

Such offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society;"
5.

Considering the aforesaid, since it is a dispute between two private parties and some of the offences registered against the petitioners, are not compoundable, but looking to the impact over the society, the offence even though not compoundable,
can be quashed in view of the compromise and settlement, if any, takes place between the parties.
6.

In view of the above, this Courts finds it a fit case in which the petition can be allowed and the proceedings pending before the trial Court in ST No. 197/22 arising against the petitioners- Sewakram, Vikas Balle, Raja Sillare and Vijay Kamde is hereby quashed.
Resultantly, all the consequential proceedings arising out of the said crime number shall also be quashed.
